School & learning

pluperfect tense noun

also pluperfect, past perfect tense, in the pluperfect

late Latin

Donatus, Ars minor, Dē verbō: praeteritum plūsquamperfectum, ut lēgeram
Traupman 226, 248

praeteritum plūsquamperfectum

the pluperfect tense

The past before the past, “more than finished”: lēgeram, I had read. Donatus’s name (fourth century), which the schools shorten to plūsquamperfectum. Lewis & Short has no entry for the tense name. In the pluperfect: tempore praeteritō plūsquamperfectō (Traupman 248).

See also tense, past tense, perfect tense, had.

SourcesLewis & Short: plus · Lewis & Short: perficio

John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency (printed page numbers): p. 226, p. 227, p. 248.
